The Arc Length of a Parametric Curve

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Write down the integral that gives the arc length of the curve  $\mathbf f (t) = \langle 3 \sin t, \: 2\sin 2t \rangle$
from $t =\dfrac {3\pi} 2$  to $t = 2\pi.$

![](images/57/574a16e843a9c81e5fc9ddbbe2c0dc2c308ffcac4991bcbf48c7f45b4871c93b.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $\mathbf f'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf f'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{f}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+16{cos}^{2}⁡2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{a}^{b}‖{f}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+16{cos}^{2}⁡2t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding an Integral Expression For the Arc Length of a Curve

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Find the arc length of the curve $\mathbf g (t) = \langle 3 - 2 \sin 2t, \: 1 - 2\cos 2t \rangle$ from $t=\dfrac \pi 3$ to $\pi.$

![](images/29/29c97e5963d451cc389944ef113764b2d15998448e773a02bb98c062207c2860.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $\mathbf g'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf g'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ ‖{g}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+(4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{cos}^{2}⁡2t+16{sin}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{a}^{b}‖{g}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi }4\,\text{d}t \\  & =4t\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{\pi } \\  & =4(\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{8\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Computing the Arc Length of a Planar Curve

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
![](images/85/8573aedcd26cba038b2db072560cd3d6ba7676542888a2d9b8a356713eaf6724.png)

Find the arc length of the curve $\mathbf r (t) = \langle \sin t ,\: \cos t, \: t \rangle$
from  $t =0$ to $t = 2\pi.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf r'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\text{ }\sqrt{2}\,t{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\sqrt{2}(2\pi -0) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
